messages:
IncidentBot: [P1] Alert: streaming tail latency spike detected across prod clusters (p99 > 10s for SSE/WebSocket). Auto-paging oncall @alex_oncall. Impact: intermittent truncated streams and client reconnects. Playbook: http://ops/playbooks/streaming-tail-latency

alex_oncall: I'm on it. pulling traces and top traces for the last 10m. any customer reports yet?

lara_support: reported from 3 customers in APAC and EU — docs-editor, voice-qa, and search-sandbox. All mention long stalls and then a chunked reconnect. I filed support tickets: TKT-4832, TKT-4833, TKT-4834.

maria_sre: initial metrics: p95 up from ~220ms -> 700ms, p99 jumping to 11s for streaming-response pipelines. Non-stream (sync) endpoints unaffected. tcp retransmits on proxy -> backend path increasing. looks like slow consumers + proxy writeback causing head-of-line.

jin_runtime: seeing lots of lines in gateway logs: ```WARN proxy: write timeout to client after 30000ms
INFO stream: buffer drained false client: 10.2.3.45
ERROR kvcache: failed to fetch prefix for req 0x7ffeed``` also a spike in worker goroutines waiting on `conn.Write` syscalls.

maria_sre: yep. pattern: client backpressure (slow reads) -> proxy buffer fills -> proxy stalls while backend keeps producing -> backpressure cascades. p99 dominated by stuck streams waiting > 10s to flush final chunk.

alex_oncall: quick mitigation ideas: 1) increase proxy write timeout to 60s as temporary (buy time) 2) enable per-connection small-chunk flush (flush_interval_ms=200) 3) route traffic for affected customers to fallback non-streaming endpoint /v1/resp/polling (degrades UX but avoids stalls) 4) scale up proxy frontends in EU/APAC. opinions?

jin_runtime: +1 to flush_interval. Code path already supports `flush_every_n_bytes` and `flush_interval_ms` toggles. Command to toggle on prod (canary first): ```curl -XPOST http://config-api/proxy/flags -d '{"flush_interval_ms":200}'``` we should canary on one AZ.

lara_support: we need comms if we route to polling. customers will want to know precise ETA and workaround steps. I can send message templates.

maria_sre: scaling proxies now. spinning +4 proxy pods in eu-west-1. also running a quick script to evict very slow socket connections (those with >30s idle write stalls) so backend can finish: ```for c in $(list-conns | grep stalled); do close-conn $c; done``` — caution: will drop some active streams.

alex_oncall: do the canary on eu-west-1-azb. jin please apply flag to that AZ, watch p99 for 5m. maria do scale +close-stalled. lara prepare customer comms and update status page. raj, do we want an automated rollback if error rate increases?

raj_product: yes update status page. put two bullet points: "Partial streaming degradation" + "Workarounds: use polling endpoint or retry". Auto-rollback: if error rate > 2% over 2m, rollback flag and remove scale change.

jin_runtime: applied to eu-west-1-azb canary: `flush_interval_ms=200`. watching logs. initial observation: p99 in canary reduced from ~9.8s -> ~1.1s (observed over 2 min). throughput stable.

maria_sre: eu-west pool scaled, stale connections evicted. overall p95 now ~330ms, p99 ~1.4s across canary region. global still higher until we roll.

alex_oncall: good signal. proceed to roll flag to eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 with staged ramp (30% -> 100% over 10min). jin coordinate. maria keep an eye on retransmits and tcp cwnd. lara prepare short advisory for affected customers: include polling fallback and recommend reconnect backoff.

lara_support: drafting now. will include the snippet for polling endpoint and example curl: ```curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streaming/polling``` also mention expected transient reconnections.

maria_sre: note for postmortem: investigate why proxy buffer growth wasn't detected earlier — add metric `proxy_writeback_queue_length` alarm at p95 threshold. also we should add instrumentation for slow consumer counts per customer-id.

jin_runtime: rolling to eu-west then apac. pushing config via config-api + restarting proxy worker process (graceful). command: ```PUT /config/proxy flush_interval_ms=200 && kubectl rollout restart ds/proxy-frontend -l region=eu-west-1```

IncidentBot: Action logged: mitigations started by alex_oncall. Incident timeline ID: INC-2024-171555.

alex_oncall: handoff summary for next oncall: cause appears to be client-side slow readers and proxy writeback not flush-friendly. Immediate mitigations: `flush_interval_ms=200` deployed canary -> rolled to eu & apac, scaled proxies +4 pods in eu, evicted stalled sockets. Customer impact: 3 known customers with truncated streams; support tickets created; status page updated. Next steps: analyze why proxies didn't flush earlier, add `proxy_writeback_queue_length` metric & alert, instrument per-customer slow-consumer counter, consider adaptive backpressure (drop-oldest-chunk) for very long tails. Oncall: alex_oncall -> handing to maria_sre in 15m.

maria_sre: taking handoff. I'll keep monitoring for 1h and start the postmortem draft. +1 to adding metrics.

lara_support: I'll send out initial comms and update tickets with workaround. will attach logs sample and recommended retries.

raj_product: thanks team. flag for product review: consider UX for polling fallback — how to make it smoother.

alex_oncall: thanks all. closing this thread for immediate action items. please add any follow-ups to INC-2024-171555. :thumbsup:
